note: Maintaining the functional subset and label correspondence is explicitly assigned to the system designer.
ParameterInterface may type P or R ports but never PR ports.
Mapping overrides ordinary compatibility only when its dependent mapping constraints hold; compile dependencies explicitly.
Exactly two distinct PortInterfaces participate in each mapping.
The connector endpoint interface pair must equal the interface pair covered by its selected mapping.
Explicit mapping has precedence and is binding for mapped-element count.
All first-side prototypes share one DataInterface owner and all second-side prototypes one other owner.
A queued element cannot map to an element with a different SwImplPolicy.
Sender-receiver element mapping requires compatible data types, an available conversion, or an explicit transformation.
Client-server argument mapping requires compatible types or an available data conversion.
Operation mapping sides must each belong to exactly one distinct ClientServerInterface.
ApplicationError mapping sides must each belong to exactly one distinct ClientServerInterface.
Every argument on both mapped operations needs a corresponding argument-mapping reference.
Mapped argument directions must be equal.
Mapped operations must own the same number of arguments.
Each argument may occur at most once on its mapping side.
Mapped mode-group prototypes must reference ModeDeclarationGroups compatible under chapter 6.7.
Mapping establishes compatibility even when mode transitions differ; dependent mapping integrity still applies.
All first modes share one group owner and all second modes one other group owner.
Mapped mode owners must equal the types referenced by firstModeGroup and secondModeGroup.
